claims.head: Don’t buy Gibson’s record against the Golden Knights
claims.body: Gibson has been a wall against the Golden Knights since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Gibson isn’t that wall tonight.

claims.head: Expect the Golden Knights to have the puck more
claims.body: The Golden Knights have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Red Wings around the middle. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Red Wings’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

DET.head: A slightly uphill night for the Red Wings
DET.body: Even though Detroit has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Red Wings’ best way to tip it is keeping shots to a minimum.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights start a half-step ahead
VGK.body: Even though Detroit has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Red Wings can still swing it if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Kolesar meets his old team
paras: The Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday, and the Red Wings (6-5-3) lost 5-4 to St. Louis on Saturday. Going in, the Golden Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Red Wings last in the Atlantic (tied for 19th).

The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.633) says: their chances are worth about .691, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Red Wings (.536 on chances worth .620), where their finishing has held them back.

The Golden Knights (1st) and the Red Wings (3rd) both draw more penalties than they take. The Golden Knights have had shaky goaltending (31st). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Red Wings’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. As for the Red Wings, they block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), but ice the puck a lot (30th). Good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Wings.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring, and Mark Stone (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Red Wings, Alex DeBrincat (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with eight points in his last five games.

John Gibson (4-5-1 / .860 SV% in 10 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Detroit, but will likely start. Vegas has two options in net: Adin Hill (5-2-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) and Carter Hart (4-3-1 / .889 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Hill got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Gibson has a .938 save percentage in six starts against the Golden Knights, well above his usual .895. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Todd McLellan likes to send Mazur, Dries and Kolesar out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Røndbjerg, Dowd and Gatcomb.
